info.bio:
Sleater-Kinney (1994 - presente) es una banda de rock alternativo formada en Olympia (Washington, EEUU), pieza clave en las escenas punk y  riot grrrl de Washington.
Su nombre viene de la calle Sleater-Kinney, en Lacey (cerca de Olympia), donde se encontraba uno de sus primeros locales de ensayo.
Los críticos Greil Marcus y Robert Christgau han elogiado a Sleater-Kinney como uno de los grupos de rock esenciales de principios de la década de 2000.

scenes.name: Foxcore y riot grrrls
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El hardcore había sido un fenómeno masculino; el movimiento «riot grrrl» introduce el «factor chica» en la ecuación de frustración, depresión, desesperación y rabia. Nace en Olympia (fanzines como «Girl Germs», el lema «Revolution Girl Style Now!») y bebe de las cantautoras neoyorquinas, las bandas femeninas californianas (Runaways, Frightwig, L7) y las británicas (Raincoats, Slits). Un movimiento fundado en las letras, no en la música: Mecca Normal, Bikini Kill de Kathleen Hanna (y luego Le Tigre), Bratmobile, Team Dresch, Hole de Courtney Love, Seven Year Bitch, Sleater-Kinney. En California, Mudwimin, 4 Non Blondes, Tribe 8, Tiger Trap, Donnas, Red Aunts, That Dog, Muffs; en el Medio Oeste, Babes In Toyland (Fontanelle, «un arte de emociones extremas») y Sugarsmack; Free Kitten y Luscious Jackson en Nueva York.
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

podcast.title: Breakup and Reunion
podcast.body: Sleater-Kinney initially broke up in 2006 but later reunited in 2014, demonstrating the lasting impact and demand for their music and message, and their continued relevance in the indie scene. "They broke up in 2006, but reunited in 2014."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Most Prolific Riot Grrrl Group
podcast.body: Among the riot grrrl groups, Sleater-Kinney is highlighted as arguably the most prolific, making them a recommended deep dive for anyone interested in 1990s punk rock. "If we had to single out one group as being the most prolific, it would probably have to be Sleeter Kinney."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musical Proficiency
podcast.body: Many contemporaries regarded Sleater-Kinney as more musically proficient than some of the earlier Riot Grrrl bands. They were known for their feminist messages and left-leaning politics, bringing a more refined musicianship to these themes. "According to a lot of the contemporaries, Slater Kinney was a little more proficient in the musician department."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Naming Origin
podcast.body: The band Sleater-Kinney was named after a road near their rehearsal space in Olympia. This detail provides a local context for their origins and connection to the Pacific Northwest scene. "Slater Kinney was formed in Olympia and named after Roboad near where the band used to rehearse."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Olympia, Washington Origins and Riot Grrrl Founders
podcast.body: Sleater-Kinney, a trio from Olympia, Washington, were among the original bands that pioneered the entire riot grrrl community. "If we had to single out one group as being the most prolific, it would probably have to be Sleeter Kinney, a trio from Olympia, Washington, and one of the originators of the entire riot girl community."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origins and History
podcast.body: A trio of women from Olympia, Washington, Sleater-Kinney became prominent within the Riot Girl indie rock scene. The band formed while Carrie Brownstein was at university, remained active for approximately twelve years, broke up in 2006, and then reformed in 2014. "a trio of women out of Olympia, Washington. ... Peter Kinney came about while she was at university. They stuck it out for about a dozen years, broke up in 2006, and then reformed in 2014."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prominent Riot Grrrl Band
podcast.body: Sleater-Kinney emerged from the Pacific Northwest as one of the biggest bands in the Riot Grrrl movement. Their music and ethos contributed significantly to the scene's influence. "The biggest of the bunch were probably Team Dresh and Sleeter Kinney, both from the Pacific Northwest."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Riot Grrrl Sensibilities in Punk Revival
podcast.body: The reformed Sleater-Kinney was cited for their "riot girl sensibilities" as part of the mid-decade punk revival in the 2010s. This revival showcased a wide variety of approaches, including Garage Punk and Post Punk, demonstrating the evolving nature of punk as an attitude and a way of life. "There was a wide variety of approaches from Laura Jane Grace and against me to the riot girl sensibilities of the reformed Slater Kinney..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Second Wave Post-Riot Grrrl Band
podcast.body: Sleater-Kinney was formed in Olympia around 1994 by Corin Tucker (formerly of Heavens to Betsy) and Carrie Brownstein. While not "exactly Riot Girls," they were deeply influenced by the movement and continued its feminist, left-leaning political messages, becoming a fixture on the American indie scene for about 10 years after the original Riot Grrrl scene faded. "One of them was Slater Kinney featuring current Tucker of Evans De Betsy and Carrie Brown Steen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Additional Musical Projects
xref.body: Beyond her work with Sleater-Kinney, Brownstein has been involved in other musical projects, including contributing to soundtracks and participating in other bands. "Oh, and there's been more music too, including some soundtracks and a couple of bands outside of Slider Kinney."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Drummer for Sleater-Kinney
xref.body: Janet Weiss is the drummer for Sleater-Kinney, an acclaimed "riot grrrl band" of the 7-O-Ride era. Her drumming is a key component of their influential sound. "There's Janet Weiss of the 7-O-Ride Girl Band's Sleeter Kinney."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

xref.title: Post-Sleater-Kinney Career
xref.body: After her time in Sleater-Kinney, Carrie Brownstein expanded her career into writing and acting. She wrote for and appeared on *Saturday Night Live* and co-created, wrote for, and starred in the Emmy-winning series *Portlandia* with Fred Armisen. She has also made appearances in *Curb Your Enthusiasm*, *Archer*, *The Simpsons*, and *Transparent*. "She later went on to write for an appearance Saturday Night Live. Maybe you've seen the Emmy award winning series she did with Fred Armason called Portlandia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

xref.title: Reunion
xref.body: Team Dresch has reunited, similar to Sleater-Kinney, showcasing the ongoing influence and activity of bands from the Riot Grrrl and post-Riot Grrrl scenes. "There have been reunions by Sleeter Kinney and Team Dresh"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Role Model Reference
xref.body: Joey Ramone is mentioned in the song "I Want to Be Your Joey Ramone" by Sleater-Kinney, which is described as a statement about girls needing female role models. This implies that while Joey Ramone was a male figure, the sentiment of the song was about finding equivalent female inspiration in the punk rock tradition. "I want to be your Joey Ramon."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
